equivalence: visibility: same answer as the base code, by the engine invariant that embedded expressions are disjoint and ascending by root (write_embedded pushes after its callback; the Python frontend appends nested candidates after the holder returns). hidden is the roots of {e : host in a hidden holder || type_position(host) != Type}, the negation of the old enabled rule, with the holder decided earlier in append order; a hidden expression nested in a visible one is decided by type_position. operand_place: Cast first operand == next(); NewType second == nth(1); TypeVar: argument is an Expression and is not the first Expression, which equals old positional > 0. ancestors stops after yielding the host's statement (service.rs:192): Slice, Subscript, CallArguments and AnnAssign never hold a statement, and embedded trees hold no statements, so nothing above the statement changes the answer. annotated_operand stops at the subscription (service.rs:267), where the old walk reached the root; both give owner != first, so Value.
residual: Accepted, no memo needed now. A left-nested chain of K string operands in one expression ('a' + 'b' + ...) still costs O(K^2) ancestor steps through completion_hosts. Measured with Python ast on the benchmark Django tree (projects/django-36b5f39d93..., django/ + tests/ + docs/ + scripts/, 2,874 files): 150,007 string constants, 435,837 steps from each to its statement (mean 2.9), maximum 20 (tests/aggregation/tests.py:1523), 16 strings at 15-19, one at 20. The ryo tree adds Extra nodes, so roughly a small constant factor more. That cost is linear in practice and far below the parse. The pathological shape exists only in generated code; it is recorded as an open item, not a memo.
